clue.text: Broadcast old woman will bear, for example

indicators.note: something broadcast goes out over the airwaves, so the words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: mother (an old woman) is MAMA, and 'will' contracts to 'll, so mama'll

explanation.surface: Someone on the radio says an old woman will bear something, by way of example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' signals that MAMA'LL, mother will, is heard as the answer. The definition hides at the end: a bear is one example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear is a warm-blooded animal that suckles its young, one instance of that class of creatures.

clue.text: Easy victory — with a sweetheart overwhelming Jack, finally

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the lover's letters close around the other piece

parts.note: a sweetheart is a lover

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word Jack

explanation.surface: A one-sided win, where a girlfriend overpowers a man named Jack in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkover is a contest won without real opposition, hence an effortless victory.

clue.text: Item of furniture in hospital everyone puts up with?

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
everyone means all
to put up with something is to stand it

explanation.surface: A piece of hospital furniture that everybody tolerates.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the whimsical surface; the definition is just the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallstand is a piece of entrance-hall furniture with hooks for coats and a rack for umbrellas.

clue.text: Someone who's rolling short strip

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: to strip someone of something is to divest them of it

explanation.surface: A person turning over and over in a brief strip of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives is the traditional name for the rich man in the parable of Lazarus, so 'rolling' means rolling in money, not tumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dives, the rich man of the Gospel parable, stands for any very wealthy person, one rolling in it.

clue.text: Stick around longing for hot condiment

indicators.note: around tells us the stick's letters surround the craving

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
a yen is a longing or craving

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about yearning for a spicy seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick around' reads as a phrase meaning stay, but it splits into a noun and a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red pepper ground into a spice used to season food.

clue.text: Lay egg having flown across river? One might

indicators.note: across tells us the jumbled letters span the river abbreviation, enclosing it
flown suggests the letters have flown off and come down in a new arrangement

parts.note: R is the standard map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A bird lays an egg after flying over a river, as one would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay egg having flown' is rearranged as GEYLAG, and 'across' puts R inside it. The definition, 'One might', refers back to the whole clue: a goose that flies over rivers and lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The greylag is a wild goose, a bird that flies over rivers and lays eggs.

clue.text: Silk fabric obtainable from Hamilton in Ontario?

indicators.note: obtainable from says the letters can be taken straight out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A silk material on sale in a Canadian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamilton is a real city in Ontario, which makes the question mark playful: the fabric sits across hamilTON IN ONtario.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer fabric, traditionally of silk, used for dresses and curtains.

clue.text: Hide plant brought back by Society family?

indicators.note: brought back means the plant's letters are turned round and read from the end

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside plant
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A Society family brings back a plant to conceal it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Deerskin is the skin of a deer, a type of animal hide used as leather.

clue.text: Costs of former opponents at table overwhelming writers

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
pens are writing implements
at the bridge table East and South are on opposing sides, abbreviated E and S

explanation.surface: The bills run up by old card-table rivals who swamp some authors.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North pairs with South and East with West, so E and S face each other as opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Expenses are the money spent on something, its costs, especially those reimbursed by an employer.

clue.text: Dab of grease initially that is needed for American's motherless calf

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A little smear of grease is needed, first of all, for an orphaned young cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dab of grease' reads as a small amount of lubricant, but 'initially' takes the first letter of all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American West a dogie is a calf that has lost its mother and runs alone in the herd.

clue.text: Master of house in Scotland with whom poor Brutus was at war?

definitions.meaning: in Scots usage the man of the house is referred to as the master of the household

definitions.text: with whom poor Brutus was at war?
definitions.meaning: in Julius Caesar, Shakespeare's Brutus is described as being at war with his own self

explanation.walkthrough: Brutus in Shakespeare says he is 'with himself at war', torn between friendship for Caesar and duty to Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots call the head of the household by the reflexive pronoun, and Brutus fought inwardly against his own person.

clue.text: Army section given large area of land to take back

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE, are a corps of the British Army
a tract is a large stretch of land

explanation.surface: An army unit is handed a big expanse of territory to recapture.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to withdraw it, to take back what was said.

clue.text: Scoffer unknown to get involved in supreme commander's retreat

indicators.note: to get involved in something is to get inside it, so one piece goes within the other
a retreat is a movement backwards, so the commander's abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: CINC is the abbreviation for commander-in-chief, the supreme commander
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so Y

explanation.surface: A mocker has no idea how to join the top general's withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' reverses CINC to CNIC, and Y goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic sneers at others' motives and goodness, a habitual scoffer.

clue.text: Productive first daughter thrown out by man in band

indicators.note: in places the man's shortened name within the band

parts.note: a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

indicators.note: thrown out means ejected, so a letter is taken away from the name

parts.note: Edward is a man's name

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter; first says it is the earlier of the name's two

explanation.surface: A fruitful outcome once the eldest girl is expelled by a male musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' removes a D, and 'first' says which: the man's name has two, and only the earlier goes. 'in' then sets what is left within the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewarding work is fruitful and gives a worthwhile return, so it is productive.

clue.text: Positive rating given courteous recognition, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are to be taken as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: an able seaman, AB, is a naval rating; a courteous recognition is a salute: AB plus SALUTE

explanation.surface: A sailor who receives a polite gesture gives a good review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Positive rating' looks like a phrase meaning a good score, but 'rating' is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To be positive about something is to be certain, and absolute likewise means complete and unqualified certainty.

clue.text: Gorge chips at first, no matter who doesn't finish

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word chips
doesn't finish means the last letter is lost

parts.note: anyone means whoever it might be, no matter who

explanation.surface: Someone eats chips first, whoever leaves them unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a verb meaning eat greedily, fitting the chips, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep narrow valley with steep sides, a gorge.

clue.text: Hairstyles chap's adopting over here in old Rome?

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the chap's letters take the others inside

parts.note: a chap is a man, and the possessive gives MANS
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
hic is the Latin word for here, the language of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A man takes on some haircuts seen here in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mohican (US: mohawk) is a strip of upright hair along the centre of a shaved head.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohicans are punk-style haircuts with the sides shaved and a central crest, so they are hairstyles.

clue.text: Singaporean, possibly, given a place in crew

indicators.note: in says the article and verb sit inside the crew word

parts.note: to crew a ship is to man it
to lay something is to place it

explanation.surface: Someone from Singapore, perhaps, is given a spot among the sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Singapore lies on the Malay peninsula and has many Malay citizens, so a Singaporean may well be described thus.

clue.text: Sound correspondence old granny kept in various cases

indicators.note: kept in means held inside, so the shuffled letters enclose the others
various suggests different forms, so the word cases is rearranged

parts.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: An elderly grandmother keeps her letters in several boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the word cases into ASSCE; 'kept in' holds the old granny inside. 'Sound' is part of the definition, a term from prosody, not a homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonance is the echo of vowel sounds between nearby words, a matching of sounds in verse.

clue.text: In state of hostility, grandad gets war wound

indicators.note: wound, as in wound up or twisted, says the letters are wrapped into a new order

explanation.surface: A veteran grandfather picks up a battle injury while the country is at war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as an injury but is the past tense of wind, twisted around.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at daggers drawn is an idiom for open enmity, ready to fight.

clue.text: Move with hawser attached — king evidently tense?

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
someone tense is on edge

explanation.surface: Moving a ship by rope, the king is obviously nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evidently' links the pieces: a king on the edge, K before EDGE, is clearly on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To kedge is to warp a ship along by hauling on a rope fixed to a small anchor.

clue.text: He wrote notes left with girl after exam

indicators.note: after places the following letters later than the exam word

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination at a university
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: Someone jotted down notes, left with a girl after a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' are musical: the definition is the composer, not someone scribbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Vivaldi was a Baroque composer, a man who wrote musical notes such as The Four Seasons.

clue.text: Rule about traders finally getting stand down?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rule word goes round the letter

parts.note: to reign is to rule

indicators.note: finally picks only the last letter of the word traders

explanation.surface: A regulation concerning merchants eventually gets an official to step aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a post, to step aside or stand down.

clue.text: Run off quickly? One may when manufacturing a car

definitions.meaning: to flee in a hurry, bolting away

definitions.text: One may when manufacturing a car
definitions.meaning: a car maker produces a dashboard for the vehicle, read as making a dash for it

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: 'dash' is short for dashboard, which a car factory makes for each car.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to bolt or flee quickly, while literally a car maker fits a dashboard to the vehicle.

clue.text: Area with auditors wandering round: there you'll get a sweat on!

definitions.text: there you'll get a sweat on!

indicators.note: wandering round suggests the letters roam about and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Accountants roam a district where things get steamy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description of a hot room rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudatoria are sweating rooms, as in Roman baths, places where one perspires.

clue.text: Figure with trendy label attached

parts.note: hep is old slang for fashionable or trendy
a tag is a label
on means attached, as in a lid that is on

explanation.surface: A design carrying a fashionable label stuck on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptagon is a seven-sided plane shape, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Grand inquisitor and cardinal rising, inspiring people with energy

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the number takes the others inside
rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: six is a cardinal number
men means people
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A top inquisitor and a church cardinal rise up, filling followers with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is a cardinal number. Cardinal Ximenes headed the Spanish Inquisition; it was also the pseudonym of a famous Observer crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal Francisco Jiménez (Ximenes) de Cisneros served as Grand Inquisitor of Spain in the early 1500s.

clue.text: Newton had a theory about it — this is serious!

definitions.text: Newton had a theory about it
definitions.meaning: Isaac Newton formulated the law of universal attraction between masses
solemn seriousness of manner or situation

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the force Newton described, the other the seriousness of a situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Newton's universal law describes the attractive force between masses, and the word also means solemn seriousness.

clue.text: Initially available, tea after church dance

indicators.note: after puts the tea word behind the others
Initially takes only the opening letter of available

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: First, if available, have tea after church and then a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom dance.

clue.text: Run rings round characters in centre of Bexley, say

indicators.note: say means the letters are to be spoken aloud, giving a word that sounds like them
centre of takes the middle pair of letters from the six-letter word Bexley

explanation.surface: A runner laps people among the residents of a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Bexley is a borough in south-east London. Its two middle letters, X and L, said aloud sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo others, and running rings round someone is an idiom for outperforming them.
